subject: Text at either end of axis

messages.author: 7a2c097f8b936c87
messages.subject: Text at either end of axis
parts:
Hello All,

I would like to have some text at either end of an axis label. For
example, on the Y-axis, I would like text at the low end to say "dry"
and the high end to say "wet".

A basic starting plot is:
ggplot(data.frame(X = runif(10), Y = runif(10)), aes(x=X, y=Y)) +
geom_point() + ylab("myVar")

I can add the text in the ylab specification, but how do I get "dry"and
"wet" appear at the far ends? It would also be nice to be able to
format the end-text differently than the text in the middle (in italics
for example).
ggplot(data.frame(X = runif(10), Y = runif(10)), aes(x=X, y=Y)) +
geom_point() + ylab("dry
myVar wet")

Any thoughts are greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Allie

messages.author: 4f04313c0a6b0f2f
messages.subject: Re: Text at either end of axis
parts:
A couple of potential starting points.

# Annotate approach: http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3/annotate.html
set.seed(123)
base=ggplot(data.frame(X = runif(10), Y = runif(10)), aes(x=X, y=Y)) +

baselabels=base +annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0:1, label = c("(dry)", "(wet)"))

baselabelsline=baselabels+annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0.01, yend = .99,
           colour = "black")

# Numeric to factor Y axis
set.seed(123)
df=data.frame(X = runif(10), Y = runif(10))
df=rbind(df,c(NA,0),c(NA,1))
df$Y=as.factor(signif(df$Y,2))
library(plyr)
df$Y=revalue(df$Y, c("0"="Dry", "1"="Wet"))
factoryplot=ggplot(df, aes(x=X, y=Y))+geom_point() + ylab("myVar")

# Also check out Winston's cookbook for axes formatting: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Axes_(ggplot2)/

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Text at either end of axis
parts:
Hi:

Here are a couple of options, including a slight modification of Vivek's reply.

p <- ggplot(data.frame(X = runif(10), Y = runif(10)), aes(x=X, y=Y)) +

p + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "Dry") +
annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1, label = "Wet")

ylabs <- c("Dry", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "Wet")
p + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.05, 1.05),
breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = ylabs)

The use of limits in scale_y_continuous is designed to ensure that the
labels on the extremes get rendered. It's a manual replacement for the
expand = argument. When I ran this, the annotated labels worked fine;
if you have a problem, consider using the hjust and/or vjust arguments
to fine tune the position of the text.

Dennis
